utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff would be pleased to address the Court to explain to you precisely the situation regarding Mr. Vujanovic and Mr. Budimir, if he may?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have been ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let me administer the oath, Mr. Wladimiroff! I am joking with you since you are sitting in the witness seat. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: May I start?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wladimiroff, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right, I have some admiration for the witnesses, your Honour, because it seems to be extremely difficult. Anyhow, we have been around to look for Mr. Vujanovic, but we could not find him so far. I will call our representative in the field at 3 o'clock, whether he will be available or not. If that is the case, he can be brought here and I expect him to be here at 4 o'clock. But at this stage I am not able to tell you whether he is available this afternoon or not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Have you been in touch with him, either you directly or your agent, the person who works with the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have not been in contact with him directly because we are here in Banja Luka and the witness is in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No one from the Defence has been able to reach him, is that what you are telling me? What I am trying to do is to find out whether we can expect him at 4.00 or whether it is a hope that if you get in touch with him he will be here at 4.00 or there at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So far, no one has been in contact with him personally, but we have been in contact with his superiors.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wladimiroff. Mr. Wladimiroff, what is the situation with Mr. Budimir? We sent two letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have to deal with your question in Serbo-Croatian, your Honour, because there is no English here, but I will try to read on the transcript in the meantime. Anyhow, we have been in contact directly with Mr. Budimir. We passed the letter of the Tribunal directly to him and he is now trying to get in contact with his superiors. At this moment he was not able to establish such a contact, but again at 3 o'clock I will call our representative who is in direct contact with him to hear what is the result of these activities. So I expect to be more informed at 3 o'clock. Also, here we are in Banja Luka and Mr. Budimir is in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He can get the train and get there in an hour or hour and a half, depending on the circumstances, I guess. Mr. Kay, Miss Hollis, or whoever is handling Mr. Vujanovic, how do you suggest that we handle this? One possibility is that we adjourn today since there has not been contact with Mr. Vujanovic so we do not know whether he will be coming this afternoon, and then also wait word after the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Interior have received the letter that I sent just early this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir you have listed for three hours. I do not know how long we need for Mr. Vujanovic, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Even if Mr. Budimir takes the full three hours, your Honour, we will still have enough time for Mr. Vujanovic tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think it may be an overestimate for Mr. Budimir, three hours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Do you agree that it is best then for us to adjourn now and reconvene tomorrow at 10.00 -- 10.30 tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would think so under the circumstances, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not mind making myself available for the rest of the afternoon. But if your Honour thinks it is not a good idea, it may be that we draw stumps for this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. We could make ourselves available, but the interpreters would have to just make themselves available and I do not see there is a need because we will have enough time tomorrow even starting at 10.30 to consider Mr. Budimir if he cannot come and Mr. Vujanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Then we will adjourn then until tomorrow at 10.30. Mr. Marro, we are adjourning until tomorrow at 10.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: (The Court adjourned until the following day)
